exactly where it stopped.
# dsh-continuechat
English | 中文
Manually resume an interrupted DeepSeek Harness conversation.
When a turn ends early — stopped by hand, cut short by a failed model request, or truncated by the o
utput-token limit — the harness leaves nothing behind but a "stopped" marker. This plugin adds the m
issing step: a `/continue` command and a **Continue** action in the action row under the interrupted
reply itself, so the run picks up exactly where it stopped instead of restarting.
## What it solves
| Situation | Without the plugin | With the plugin |

| You hit stop by accident | Retype "continue" yourself | Click **Continue** |
| A network or provid
er failure aborted the turn | Restate the context before the model resumes | The plugin hands the re

corded failure to the model and resumes |
| The reply was cut off by the token limit | The harness s
ays *send "continue"* — with no entry point | One click or one command continues the answer |
## Usage
### Command
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Text after the command name is appended to the continuation prompt as an "Additional instruction fro
mmand name is appended to the continuation prompt as an "Additional instruction from the user" line.
The command's outcome (`已请求继续对话（中断原因：手动停止）。`) is rendered by the harness command plane; it never bec
omes a model message.
### Button
On the turn that was cut short, a **Continue** action appears in the action row under the closing as
sistant message — the same row that carries copy / thumbs-up / thumbs-down / branch:
- **It only appears on a real interruption.** Turns that completed, were blocked, or merely closed a

fork show nothing, so the button never shows up under a conversation that ended normally.
- Only th
e assistant message that closes that turn carries it; every other message renders nothing and takes

no space.
- It disappears again once the agent is running.
- Clicking it is exactly one `/continue`

execution.
- A failed attempt keeps a short error line next to the action (hover for the full text).
The decision comes from the session's durable event window: the newest `turn/end` must have a resuma
ble reason *and* that turn must carry a **persistent** assistant message. A turn that was interrupte
d **before producing any assistant output** (a request that failed outright, a process that died bef
ore streaming) therefore has nowhere to host the button — use the `/continue` command there.
### Command menu
Type `/` and pick `continue` ("Continue the interrupted conversation from where it stopped"). Arrow
keys plus Enter are enough — no draft typing required.
## How it works
### Interruption tracking (host half)
The plugin subscribes to the session log's `session/event` and tracks every turn end:
[该节后续省略]
### Why the answer is a separate message
After you press **Continue**, DSH opens a new turn for the model to write on, and the plugin then re
tires that turn's trigger prompt from the transcript — so you no longer see the prompt, and the inte
rrupted reply is followed directly by the new text.
The retirement is a `system/message` replacement, and the log makes such an event *step-scoped*: its
`turn`/`step` must name the step that is open as it lands, and both coordinates must be positive (`
dsh-session-format-v3-to-v4/lib/index.js`, `assertV4SystemMessageFields` plus the relationship repla
y). A turn that has already ended names no open step, so the replacement cannot be written there. It
rides the step that produced the model's answer to the prompt — or, for a turn that produced none,
the next step that opens.
The new text **cannot be merged into the original message**. That is an architectural constraint of
the DSH session log, not an implementation shortcut:
- The log is event-sourced: a committed assistant message cannot be edited, only shadowed by a surfa

ce `replace`.
- A `replace` must list every shadowed node in `sourceEventSeqs` (`dsh-session/lib/ind
ex.js:327`), while `assistant/message` is explicitly forbidden from carrying that field (`:313`, it
embeds its provider stream). The two rules conflict, so no assistant event can perform a replacement

.
- Shadowing the whole range with a `system/message` instead would also shadow the `tool/call` / `t
ool/result` pairs inside it, breaking the model history so the next request fails.
The provider side has no assistant prefill either (`dsh-llm-deepseek` carries only anthropic-beta fl
ags), so the model cannot literally continue the previous assistant message — it must generate a new
so the model cannot literally continue the previous assistant message — it must generate a new one.
The result: **no stray "continue" prompt, but still a separate new answer.**
## What it deliberately does not do
- **It never continues on its own.** Every trigger is human: a command, the button, or your own typi

ng. For automatic continuation use the `goal` tool.
- **It never shows the button under a normally f
inished conversation.** The decision comes straight from the session log's `turn/end` reason, not fr

om a guess about which turn is last.
- **It never merges the new answer into the previous message.**
That is impossible in this architecture (see above); the continuation is always a new assistant mes

sage, and the plugin only retires its own trigger prompt.
- **It never cuts in while the agent runs.

** `/continue` against a running agent reports an error instead; stop the turn first.
- **It never r

ewrites history.** A continuation is one new user message appended to the log.
- **It never retires
a prompt outside an open step.** The replacement is written from inside the step that answers the pr
ompt, or from the next step that opens when a turn ends without an answer. That is the only position

the log accepts, and it is why the retirement is not part of the `turn/end` handling.
- **It never
replays the session log.** The plugin only observes events appended inside the current process, so t
he first `/continue` after a **DSH restart** reports "未记录中断原因" and falls back to the generic prompt

— the resume still works, it just loses the reason detail.
- **It ships zero runtime dependencies.**
The host half imports only `node:crypto`; the client half requires only `react` from the platform s
eed table. No build step, no `node_modules`.
